Timeline::year_scalar¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

int Timeline::year_scalar() const

Read One Civil Year As A C++ Value¶

year_scalar() extracts the year displayed for one scalar instant in the Timeline’s current timezone. It returns an ordinary int, which makes it the direct choice for control flow, scalar validation, and C++ APIs that do not accept a Series.

The receiver must be rank zero. A one-element vector still has rank one and is rejected; element count does not erase shape. Use year() for any array-shaped Timeline. That method preserves shape and returns a Series, whereas year_scalar() deliberately proves that exactly one scalar instant is being consumed.

The result is a civil field, not a property of the stored UTC tick alone. Changing tz() can move an instant across midnight or New Year and therefore change the answer without changing the instant.

Example: Leap-Year Date¶

const auto leap_day = pluss::timeline::make("2024-02-29T23:45:00Z");
std::cout << leap_day.year_scalar() << '\n';

Output¶

2024

Example: The Same Instant In Two Civil Years¶

const auto utc = pluss::timeline::make("2025-01-01T01:30:00Z");
const auto edmonton = utc.tz_convert("America/Edmonton");

std::cout << "UTC=" << utc.year_scalar() << '\n'
          << "Edmonton=" << edmonton.year_scalar() << '\n';

Output¶

UTC=2025
Edmonton=2024

This is not truncation or reparsing. Both values identify the same instant; their active civil calendars place it on opposite sides of New Year.

Example: Absent Instant And Rank Failure¶

const auto nat = pluss::timeline::make("");
std::cout << "absent=" << nat.year_scalar() << '\n';

const auto one_vector = pluss::timeline::make({"2024-02-29T23:45:00Z"});
try {
  static_cast<void>(one_vector.year_scalar());
  std::cout << "accepted\n";
} catch (const std::exception&) {
  std::cout << "one-element vector rejected\n";
}

Output¶

absent=-1
one-element vector rejected

-1 is the absent-field sentinel. Test isnat_scalar() before extraction when absence must not be confused with an integer result.

Contract Summary¶

  • The receiver must be rank zero, including for NaT.

  • The active timezone determines the civil year.

  • The method allocates an internal scalar projection but returns an int.

  • It does not mutate the Timeline or discard nanosecond precision from it.

  • NaT returns -1; non-scalar input throws.

See Also¶

  • year(): shape-preserving year extraction.

  • week(): ISO week number, which can belong to an adjacent week-year.

  • tz_convert(): change the civil view without changing instants.
